questions_verbatim.1: Q1. Distinguish logical file size, HDFS block size and replication factor. Why does this single-DataNode setup not demonstrate fault tolerance?
questions_verbatim.2: Q2. Why use userId as the Kafka key? What ordering guarantee does Kafka provide, and what guarantee does it not provide across three partitions?
questions_verbatim.3: Q3. Compare the logical input record counts and the query results from CSV and Parquet. Why must these match?
questions_verbatim.4: Q4. Explain your measured runtime results. Do not claim that Parquet is always faster: consider schema inference, caching, Spark startup and this small dataset.
questions_verbatim.5: Q5. What changes in the execution plan and totalDocsExamined? Explain why a selective lookup benefits from an index even if elapsed time changes very little.
questions_verbatim.6: Q6. Does Presto copy the entire MongoDB collection into its own permanent storage? Describe the roles of Presto (query engine), MongoDB (data source) and the connector.
questions_verbatim.7: Q7. Suppose you rerun the JSON import without clearing the MongoDB collection or using idempotent upserts. What can go wrong? Propose a practical way to make the import repeatable.
questions_verbatim.8: Q8. Compare the five technologies by their roles in this homework. Which components provide durable storage, message transport, computation and interactive querying? Identify one important limitation of this simplified single-machine deployment.
